issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s deposit of rent arrears through a general court-deposit mechanism is a valid tender when the receiving court is also exercising rent-control jurisdiction.
material_facts: The tenants deposited rent owed to the landlord in court under a provision allowing a person who owes money to deposit it for the creditor.
The court receiving the deposit was presided over by a judge who also functioned as the rent controller for the area.
The landlord was informed of the deposit, which was available for withdrawal.
issues.conclusion: The deposit was a valid tender of the rent arrears for the purposes of the rent-control law.
issues.legal_principle: The broad wording of Section 31 of the Punjab Relief of Indebtedness Act, 1934 covers any person who owes money, including a tenant owing rent. Read with the notification appointing subordinate judges as controllers and the relevant Punjab Courts Act arrangements, Section 31 provides machinery for receiving money for creditors; a qualifying deposit is treated as a deposit to the landlord’s credit. The Court followed Kuldip Singh v. The State of Punjab, Mam Chand v. Chhotu Ram, and Khushi Ram v. Shanti Rani, and overruled Vidya Prachar Trust v. Pandit Basarat Ram.

rule.if: rent_eviction_proceeding and tenant_owed_rent_arrears and deposited_for_creditor_in_dual_function_court and creditor_notified_of_deposit

predicates.rent_eviction_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking eviction of a tenant on the ground of unpaid rent.
predicates.tenant_owed_rent_arrears: The tenant owed rent arrears to the landlord.
predicates.deposited_for_creditor_in_dual_function_: The tenant deposited the arrears in court for the landlord, and the receiving court was also exercising rent-control jurisdiction.
predicates.creditor_notified_of_deposit: The creditor was informed that the deposited money was available for withdrawal.
predicates.rent_deposit_is_valid_tender: The rent deposit counts as a valid tender of the arrears.

issues.definition: When a rent-eviction proceeding concerns rent arrears deposited for the creditor in a court also exercising rent-control jurisdiction, and the creditor is notified, the deposit counts as a valid tender.

issues.legal_issue: Depositing future rent does not invalidate a tenant’s tender when no fair rent has been fixed.
material_facts: The tenant deposited future rent along with rent already due.
No fair rent had been fixed by the controller.
The landlord could withdraw only the rent in arrears and leave the future rent deposited.
issues.conclusion: There was no bar to depositing future rent, and the deposit did not make the tender invalid.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 6 and 19 of the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949 restrict advance rent in the circumstances covered by Section 6, including where fair rent has been fixed; they do not bar the deposit of future rent where no fair rent has been fixed. The landlord may take only the arrears and leave future rent untouched.

predicates.rent_eviction_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking eviction of a tenant on the ground of unpaid rent.
predicates.no_fair_rent_fixed: The controller had not fixed a fair rent for the premises.
predicates.tenant_deposited_future_rent: The tenant deposited rent for a period beyond the rent already due.
predicates.future_rent_deposit_does_not_invalidate_: The deposit of future rent does not make the tender invalid.

issues.definition: In a rent-eviction proceeding, if fair rent has not been fixed and the tenant deposits future rent, that deposit does not invalidate the tender.

issues.legal_issue: Payment of the rent arrears, interest, and costs on or before the first hearing satisfies the tenant’s payment condition even if the arrears were deposited earlier.
material_facts: The tenants deposited the arrears of rent before the eviction proceeding was filed and deposited future rent as well.
The tenants paid the interest and costs on the first hearing.
The deposited arrears and the payment of interest and costs were available to the landlord by the first hearing.
issues.conclusion: The tenants complied with the payment condition and were protected from eviction for default; the eviction suit had to be dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The proviso to Section 13(2) of the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949 requires the rent arrears, interest, and assessed costs to be paid or tendered on or before the first hearing. Its protective purpose must not be frustrated by a hypertechnical construction; an earlier deposit that remains available to the landlord suffices. The Court applied Sheo Narain v. Sher Singh.

rule.if: rent_eviction_proceeding and rent_default_alleged and arrears_interest_and_costs_paid_or_deposited_by_first_hearing and payment_available_to_landlord

predicates.rent_eviction_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking eviction of a tenant on the ground of unpaid rent.
predicates.rent_default_alleged: The landlord alleged that the tenant had defaulted in paying rent.
predicates.arrears_interest_and_costs_paid_or_depos: The tenant paid or deposited all rent arrears, interest, and assessed costs no later than the first hearing.
predicates.payment_available_to_landlord: The money paid or deposited was available to the landlord by the first hearing.
predicates.tenant_satisfies_payment_condition_and_i: The tenant has met the payment condition and is protected from eviction on the ground of rent default.

issues.definition: If a landlord seeks eviction for rent default and the tenant makes all required payments by the first hearing with the money available to the landlord, the tenant meets the payment condition and is protected from default-based eviction.
